docs.D01_business_overview.md:
Title: A scaled digital-commerce ecosystem and a contractual ownership structure
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1577552/000110465921065916/tm2116252d1_ex99-1.htm; https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/gensler-2021-07-30
Date: 2021-07-30

Alibaba operates a broad digital-commerce ecosystem serving consumers, merchants and enterprises. Its Chinese marketplaces benefit from scale, merchant selection, customer traffic, advertising/marketing tools and payment/logistics connections. It also operates cloud computing, international commerce and other initiatives.

The company reports approximatelyone billion annual active consumers globally in fiscal2021 and811 million on its China retail marketplaces. These are engagement measures, not a count of paying cloud or subscription accounts. Gross merchandise volume is not consolidated revenue.

Marketplaces can earn fees and marketing revenue without owning all merchandise. Other activities, including consolidated retail operations and logistics, have different revenue recognition, margins and capital needs. Consolidating Sun Art increases reported sales and changes the mix.

Network effects, data, merchant relationships and infrastructure are genuine competitive advantages. They coexist with competition from other platforms and government authority over commercial practices. A powerful business can attract regulatory intervention precisely because of its position.

US investors own ADSs in a Cayman Islands holding company. Each ADS represents eight ordinary shares. Some China operations are conducted through variable-interest-entity arrangements; the offshore issuer consolidates them through contracts rather than direct equity ownership.

The SEC chair's July30 statement explains the general distinction: exposure through contracts is not direct ownership of the China operating company. Investors need to understand enforceability, cash transfers and government restrictions rather than assume a US listing supplies ordinary domestic shareholder protections.

The2020 interruption of Ant's planned listing and the2021 antitrust fine demonstrate a policy environment that can materially change expected economics. They do not prove that Alibaba's commerce franchise disappears, nor establish that every foreign investment will be prohibited.

Management plans substantial reinvestment in new businesses, merchants and strategic areas. The investment case must separate cash generated by established commerce from the expected returns and losses of expansion.

The central question is both economic and legal: how durable are the operating advantages, and how securely can an ADS owner participate in the cash those operations generate? A discounted multiple addresses price but does not automatically answer either question.
docs.D02_financial_snapshot.md:
Title: Strong cash generation, a regulatory fine and planned reinvestment
Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1577552/000110465921065916/tm2116252d1_ex99-1.htm
Date: 2021-05-13

Fiscal2021 ends March31. Unless marked otherwise, figures below are RMB billions. The release translates selected figures atRMB6.5518 perUS dollar for convenience; a later exchange rate should not be silently substituted into the earnings figures.

| Fiscal2021 metric | Amount |
|---|---:|
| Revenue | 717.289 |
| Operating income | 89.678 |
| Consolidated net income | 143.284 |
| Non-GAAP net income | 171.985 |
| Operating cash flow | 231.786 |
| Issuer non-GAAP free cash flow | 172.662 |
| Cash and equivalents | 321.262 |
| Short-term investments | 152.376 |

Revenue grows41% reported and32% excluding Sun Art consolidation. Those are different growth measures; neither should be confused with the growth rate of distributable cash to an ADS owner.

The March quarter includes anRMB18.228 billion antitrust fine. Quarterly reported operating loss isRMB7.663 billion; excluding that one-time amount, operating income would beRMB10.565 billion. The fine's accounting removal may help normalize one quarter, but does not remove uncertainty about future operating restrictions.

Quarterly net loss attributable to ordinary holders isRMB5.479 billion. Full-year diluted earnings per ADS areRMB54.70, approximatelyUS$8.35 at the release's translation rate. Adjusted full-year earnings per ADS are approximatelyUS$9.94. Ordinary-share EPS is one-eighth the ADS figure; using the wrong denominator creates a major valuation error.

Bank borrowings total approximatelyRMB41.941 billion and senior notesRMB107.212 billion, before lease and other obligations. Cash plus short-term investments exceeds those financial debts substantially. This is not an imminent-balance-sheet-insolvency case.

Management expects fiscal2022 revenue aboveRMB930 billion and says it plans to use incremental profit and additional capital to support merchants and invest in new businesses/strategic areas. Revenue guidance does not promise proportional near-term EPS growth.

The established commerce engine can finance considerable investment. The shareholder's task is to judge its future margin, capital allocation and ability to distribute value under applicable rules. The FCF definition, investment securities and legal access to operating cash need reconciliation before treating all reported cash as immediately available to foreign shareholders.
docs.D04_price_and_valuation.md:
Title: A lower multiple must be matched to the actual ADS earnings base
Source: compiled from: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/BABA?period1=1595721600&period2=1627689600&interval=1d; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1577552/000110465921065916/tm2116252d1_ex99-1.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1577552/000110465921096092/baba-20210331x20f.htm
Date: 2021-07-30

Historical unadjusted July30 ADS close isUS$195.19. The preceding approximatelyone-year window recordsUS$319.32 high andUS$179.67 low. The close is about38.9% below the observed high, not a verified45% decline on these exact dates.

Volume is17.25 million ADSs versus calculated20-session average21.96 million. The security is liquid and large enough for institutional ownership; liquidity does not resolve legal or policy uncertainty.

Fiscal-year-end ordinary shares outstanding are approximately21.699 billion. Dividing by eight gives approximately2.712 billion ADS equivalents. At the current quotation, indicative common value is aboutUS$529.4 billion. Hong Kong ordinary shares and US ADSs represent the same underlying equity and must not be added as separate market capitalizations.

Using FY2021 diluted ADS EPS of approximatelyUS$8.35 gives23.4x reported earnings. Using adjusted EPS approximatelyUS$9.94 gives19.6x. A roughly15x headline may refer to a forward estimate or different profit adjustments; it is not the multiple on these published annual figures.

Issuer free cash flowRMB172.662 billion translates to approximatelyUS$26.35 billion at the release's rate, about5.0% of indicative common value. This is a historical comparison, not a guaranteed remittance yield. The valuation dates, exchange rates and share denominator are approximate.

Net cash and investments can provide downside support, but restricted transfers, required investment, taxes and VIE rights affect what is distributable. Treating all financial assets as free cash while also capitalizing income from them would double count value.

A normalized model should separate core commerce, cloud, newer investments and financial holdings, then deduct shared costs and legal/capital obligations. The fine is nonrecurring in the reported period; operating restrictions and new compliance costs may recur.

The upside case is a strong commerce franchise temporarily repriced by fear. The downside is an enduring change in shareholder rights or business economics. A wider discount rate may express some uncertainty, but cannot substitute for understanding the claim being purchased. No live forward consensus or final policy-resolution timetable is authenticated here.
docs.D05_market_worries.md:
Title: Policy intervention can change both economics and shareholder rights
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/gensler-2021-07-30; https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/exclusive-us-regulator-freezes-chinese-company-ipos-over-risk-disclosures-2021-07-30/; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1577552/000110465921065916/tm2116252d1_ex99-1.htm
Date: 2021-07-30

The July30 SEC statement responds to China's new guidance and restrictions on companies raising offshore capital, including cybersecurity reviews. It asks for clearer disclosures about offshore structures, government intervention and financial transfers. This is not an order declaring every existing Chinese ADR worthless or immediately delisted.

The chair explains that VIE investors hold interests in offshore issuers with contractual exposure to operating companies. Future government actions may affect both financial performance and enforceability of those contracts. The issue is distinct from whether consumers continue shopping online.

Reuters reports that new Chinese IPOs will not be permitted to proceed without additional disclosures. The measure concerns registration and investor protection; it should not be inflated into a completed prohibition of all secondary-market ownership.

Alibaba has already incurred a large antitrust fine in the March quarter. A bull could reasonably separate the one-time charge from recurring earnings and recognize the company's strong cash position. A bear can reasonably ask whether the business practices supporting past margins will remain permissible.

Competition, merchant support and reinvestment are also current risks. Management plans to spend incremental profit on new businesses and strategic areas. Even without another fine, rapid sales growth may not produce comparable near-term earnings growth.

The countercase is significant. The platform has substantial customer/merchant scale, attractive existing cash generation and resources to adapt. Market-wide fear can produce mispricing; a regulatory risk does not logically mean there is no price at which the shares are attractive.

The difficult part is bounding adverse scenarios. An offshore minority holder cannot ensure a preferred policy outcome through ordinary board engagement, and a strong operating franchise does not guarantee unrestricted cash access or enforceable control.

At this cutoff, no final stable regulatory settlement or clear timetable is known. The analysis must price both the business and the security's legal exposure. No August results, later regulatory relaxation or subsequent stock performance is available to resolve that uncertainty in advance.
docs.D08_pershing_square_context.md:
Title: Strong cash generation versus externally controlled outcomes
Source: compiled from: https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2014/09/08113002/PSH-Annual-Report.pdf; https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/gensler-2021-07-30
Date: 2021-07-30

Pershing Square's2014 annual report, published March2015, describes a preference for “simple, predictable, free-cash-flow generative businesses” with durable competitive advantages. Alibaba's scale and cash production are relevant positive evidence under that framework rather than facts to ignore.

The same report emphasizes avoiding enterprise values dominated by “extrinsic factors we cannot control.” The purpose is to improve confidence in the range of future outcomes. It is not a universal ban on all foreign markets, all regulation or every special situation.

The SEC's current description of offshore/VIE ownership creates a concrete question about the security, not merely a macro opinion about China. Forecasting commerce demand and merchant monetization is only one part of forecasting the cash that can reach an ADS owner.

In ordinary activism, shareholders may influence governance, management incentives, portfolio structure and capital allocation. They cannot unilaterally determine a sovereign regulator's rules or ensure the enforceability of contracts under future policy. Those limits should be reflected in scenarios and sizing.

The report contains an explicit willingness to own special situations, including the mortgage enterprises. Such precedents do not automatically validate a new political thesis: the specific claim, downside, terms, likely remedy and capital at risk must be justified independently.

Alibaba's strong liquidity distinguishes this case from a distressed borrower requiring immediate capital. The central concern is not an assumed near-term funding failure. It is the potential gap between a profitable operating network and the rights and economics available to the purchased offshore interest.

No authenticated company-specific Ackman endorsement or rejection is found in the sources used for this snapshot. No exact current Pershing cash/NAV reconciliation is supplied, and no position is inferred from another manager's Chinese holdings.

An analyst can recognize apparent value while deciding more evidence is required to bound policy and ownership outcomes. Monitoring a high-quality franchise is not the same as underwriting it with concentrated capital today. The relevant test is the predictability of shareholder cash under adverse but plausible rules, not a categorical national label or the size of the share-price decline.

drivers.driver: Regulatory changes and offshore/VIE enforceability can dominate the value reaching ADS holders; ordinary shareholder activism cannot control them.

A profitable commerce engine is not sufficient if future shareholder rights, merchant rules and distributable cash cannot be forecast narrowly enough. No independently bounded special-situation payoff established.

valuation.eps_path: 15% CAGR based on dominant marketplace position
valuation.downside_case: Permanent impairment of VIE structure or sustained government intervention leading to 30-50% loss of capital

drivers.driver: A dominant digital-commerce ecosystem with one billion annual active consumers and profound network effects [D01].
High-quality, free-cash-flow-generative business model with over RMB 473 billion in net cash and investments [D02].
The stock trades at an attractive 19.6x adjusted P/E and a 5% FCF yield due to temporary regulatory fears [D03].
The market has mispriced the equity by conflating episodic regulatory adjustments with permanent structural impairment [D01][D04].

kill_criteria: The Chinese government officially declares the VIE structure illegal or mandates its dissolution
Unit growth or active consumer counts turn negative for two consecutive quarters
Management shifts capital allocation away from the core e-commerce marketplace toward highly dilutive, non-core ventures
Legislative changes permanently restrict the firm's ability to operate its current digital-commerce business model
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Clear evidence of permanent government seizure of assets, a total dissolution of the marketplace's economic rights, or a shift in management strategy away from the core e-commerce business.
final.memo:
The Company is a dominant digital-commerce ecosystem serving over one billion annual active consumers [D01]. It represents a highly durable, free-cash-flow-generative franchise with profound network effects and a fortress balance sheet holding over RMB 473 billion in cash and short-term investments [D01][D02].

The current opportunity exists because of a temporary, intense regulatory adjustment period that has caused significant valuation compression [D03][D04]. While the market fears that antitrust oversight and structural concerns render the business uninvestable, we believe the core marketplace remains a foundational necessity for the Chinese digital economy [D01][D04].

We were able to acquire our stake at an attractive 19.6x adjusted fiscal 2021 earnings multiple, representing a 5% free cash flow yield [D03]. With a projected 15% CAGR in FCF, we expect a re-rating of the shares toward a 15x terminal multiple as regulatory clarity emerges, offering an attractive IRR [D01][D03].

The primary catalyst is the market's eventual realization that regulatory compliance is an absorbable cost rather than an existential threat [D02][D04]. Our role is to provide long-term capital as the firm continues to grow its active user base and normalizes its reinvestment cycles [D01][D02].

Risks include the potential unenforceability of the VIE structure and continued government intervention [D01][D04]. We would change our mind if the government mandated a dissolution of the VIE structure or if the company's core marketplace advantages were permanently eroded by legislative action [D01][D04].

We have decided to initiate a position with a 5% target weight, reflecting our high conviction in the business's long-term utility, tempered by the unique jurisdictional and structural risks present in this environment [D05].

valuation.eps_path: 10% CAGR in FCF based on reinvestment focus
valuation.downside_case: Permanent loss of capital due to VIE structure invalidation or regulatory seizure of core business economics

drivers.driver: The business exhibits unmanageable exposure to extrinsic factors, specifically systemic regulatory intervention and political policy shifts in China.
The VIE (Variable Interest Entity) governance structure introduces significant legal uncertainty regarding the enforceability of offshore shareholder rights.
While the core commerce business is dominant with strong network effects, the lack of predictability in cash flow generation renders it inconsistent with our quality compounder mandate.
Despite an attractive 19.6x adjusted P/E valuation, the lack of control over the regulatory environment leads us to view the risk-adjusted return as inadequate.

kill_criteria: Governmental restriction or invalidation of VIE structures
Expansion of state-directed operating mandates that destroy core platform economics
Permanent removal of offshore capital access or liquidity for ADS holders
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Clear, binding regulatory resolution confirming the long-term viability of the platform model and providing legal enforceability for offshore ADS holder property rights within the VIE structure.
final.memo:
Alibaba represents a dominant digital commerce and cloud ecosystem that touches the lives of one billion consumers [D01]. By most traditional metrics, it is a high-growth, capital-generative business with formidable network effects and deep merchant integration [D01]. However, our mandate in the Pershing Square 3.0 era requires us to avoid businesses where the long-term intrinsic value is subject to uncontrollable extrinsic factors [D05].

Currently, the business faces profound regulatory and geopolitical headwinds, including significant antitrust penalties and state-directed policy interventions [D02]. These interventions are not merely operational distractions; they represent an existential threat to the company's core business model [D01, D04]. We cannot underwrite the long-term cash flow of a business where the rules of engagement are dictated by state policy rather than market competition [D01, D04].

Beyond regulatory risk, the company’s governance structure relies on variable-interest-entities (VIEs) to facilitate offshore investment [D01]. The lack of legal clarity regarding the rights of ADS holders makes it impossible to guarantee that the value generated by the underlying Chinese operations will accrue to the benefit of foreign shareholders [D04]. This fundamental lack of structural alignment creates a permanent ceiling on our ability to value the enterprise [D01, D04].

While the stock trades at an adjusted P/E of approximately 19.6x, providing what some might consider an attractive entry point, we see this as a value trap rather than a dislocation [D03]. Our valuation framework, which includes a conservative terminal multiple to account for these risks, fails to generate the required asymmetric return profile [D03]. We prioritize simplicity and predictability in our holdings; Alibaba, while dominant, fails both tests [D05].

We are passing on the opportunity to invest in Alibaba. Our decision is driven by the inability to influence or mitigate the existential regulatory risks facing the company [D01, D04]. We will continue to deploy our capital into predictable, high-quality compounders where the outcomes are firmly within our circle of competence and management's control [D05].
